text:
Maya: FYI I ran a quick bring-up for Topiary v1.2 (256-d, per-channel quant6). Good throughput win (~1.7x vs fp16) but recall@10 on wiki-holdout dropped from 0.872 -> 0.830 (~4.2% absolute). posting here.
Juan: can you share which cohorts/splits? is it uniform or tail-heavy?
Maya: split breakdown in the short summary: short queries (<=8 tokens) down most, long-tail cohort also worse. silhouette avg dropped ~0.05, mean cosine shift ~0.018.
Sam: 4pts is pretty large. did you track anchor/neighborhood stability?
Anya: ran neighbor-consensus (k=10) on a sample: anchor-flip rate ~9% overall, ~12% in long-tail. that maps to the recall drop pattern.
Maya: uploaded UMAP snapshots to the internal dashboard (internal/report/Topiary-v1.2-umap) — you can see cluster drift around two dense clusters.
Sam: I want to try triage steps: (A) per-tensor int6 sweep (B) post-quant calibration (C) cosine-normalize vectors before indexing (D) neighbor-consensus at k=1,5,10 to profile where flips occur. I'll kick off A + D.
ci-bot: embed-eval pipeline triggered by @Sam (job e-8721). Runs: wiki-holdout, cohorts=[short,long,tail]. Metrics: recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,neighbor-consensus,silhouette. ETA ~30m.
Juan: small thing — are we indexing raw vectors or normalized ones? quant noise interacts with L2 vs cosine differently.
Anya: index currently built from raw vectors. quick normalize-to-unit sample recovered ~1.6% recall on a smoke check.
Maya: low-friction mitigations to try in parallel: - index-time normalization - hybrid-index (store anchors or top-N as fp16, rest quantized) - per-index rerank on top-k
Sam: command I'm running for the sweep:
```
./tools/embed-eval \
  --model topiary:v1.2 \
  --quant perchannel6 \
  --holdout wiki \
  --cohorts short,long,tail \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,neighbor-consensus,silhouette \
  --seed 42
```
Maya: decision for now: DO NOT promote Topiary-quant6 to staging. if per-tensor6 or normalization recovers >2% recall we'll re-evaluate canary. also track latency/cost tradeoffs so we don't lose the reason to quantize.
Juan: I can run a hybrid-index smoke on dedicated nodes if you want to test quickly.
Sam: will post sweep results back here in ~35m. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks — if sweep shows flips concentrated at k<=5 we can opt for normalization + rerank as a fast rollback. syncing tomorrow 10am PT in #eng-ml if needed.
